answer: A harbor registry admits an agent only for one unique data shard filed under its own key. A jade tag seals that shard to the key, so the same bytes cannot serve twice. Each epoch the registry challenges the identity through its inlet; a missed or wrong proof burns its 70-credit bond. The k-th fake needs a fresh shard, inlet, and 70 credits, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 shards and 70,000 credits, while an honest agent keeps one shard and 70 credits. A rented-shard ring fails: two identities presenting one shard trigger duplicate custody and both bonds burn.
